title: Known physics is recovered by a ladder of admissibility conditions

statements.text: Starting from the conserved current, each further admissibility condition (finite propagation, observer comparison, covariance, locality, stress redistribution, divergence-compatible closure, finite recoverability) is needed because the previous structure fails under non-uniform redistribution. The ladder reconstructs known physics as the minimal lawful completion at each step, and does not deduce it from continuity alone.

sources.quote: The manuscript does not claim that continuity alone exhaustively derives modern physics.
Each successive layer becomes necessary because the preceding structure becomes insufficient to preserve lawful comparison under non-uniform redistribution.
